messages:
Alex K: FYI support ticket from AcmePlatform — they've been seeing p95/p99 spikes on production for the Dedicated EU pool since ~09:10 UTC. Said user-facing endpoints are timing out (30s) a few times in the last hour. Escalated to us for root cause and ETA. attaching quick summary.

Emily Z: copying the customer notes: 'We started getting intermittent 504s, then a lot of 2-3s responses that used to be <200ms. Affects bulk inference and chat endpoints. Happened after a busy morning batch job.' They included a sample request id: r-7b9f2c.

Oncall Bot: INCIDENT created: INC-2026-0315-41 — Dedicated EU pool latency increase. Pager duty: @oncall.

Maria P: looking at metrics now — p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~480ms around 09:08, p99 up to ~1.4s. Request rate increased ~2.8x due to customer batch run starting at 09:00. Autoscaler didn't add capacity until ~09:14. That's a 6 min scale-up lag.

Ryan C: any pod failures in the pool? A cold GPU start could add ~500-900ms per request if KV cache cold + driver load.

Jordan M: checked cluster events: several nodes were marked NotReady while provisioning. Cloud logs show instance provisioning delays 'instance_attach_timeout' for about 3 nodes. Also kubelet reported imagePullBackOff on 2 nodes for ~30s. Looks like multiple things aligned.

Maria P: here's the quick timeline I pulled from metrics/cluster logs:
- 09:00: batch job starts, 3x baseline qps
- 09:06: pool maxed at 85% concurrency, queue depth rises
- 09:08: p95 jumps
- 09:14: autoscaler triggered new instances (scale decision at 09:09 but nodes ready at 09:14-09:16)
- 09:20: request latency back to ~180ms as new nodes warm up

Sara L: was there a recent autoscaler policy change? I remember we adjusted the cooldown last month.

Maria P: yes we lowered min_replicas for EU to save cost last week (min=1 -> min=0) and reduced max surge pre-pulls. That makes cold-start worse for bursty workloads.

Emily Z: customer says this is blocking some SLA-sensitive endpoints. They want mitigation and prevention.

Ryan C: reproduce steps to verify cold-start impact:
1) set pool min_replicas=0 for a short window
2) send synthetic burst to reach 3x rps
3) observe scale decision lag and node readiness time

I ran a quick sim in staging — with min=0 I see >5s tail latency for first wave of requests due to image pull + driver init. With min=1 it drops to <400ms.

Alex K: paste of relevant logs (trimmed):

```
Mar 15 09:10:12 cloud-api instance-manager: provision instance i-0a1b2c3d status=starting
Mar 15 09:11:01 kubelet i-0a1b2c3d: pulling image registry.redwood/inference:v2.3
Mar 15 09:11:34 kubelet i-0a1b2c3d: imagePullBackOff
Mar 15 09:12:25 kubelet i-0a1b2c3d: container start
Mar 15 09:12:55 gpu-driver init: probing devices
Mar 15 09:13:10 inference-server: model artifact load 0.9s, kv cache warm 1.1s
Mar 15 09:13:45 inference-server: ready
```

Jordan M: cloud side also had transient AZ throttling which bumped provisioning by ~60s. Combined with image pull and driver init, that explains the 6-8min window.

Maria P: root cause: dedicated pool configured for cost-optimization (min_replicas=0, reduced pre-pull), combined with a bursty customer job and transient cloud provisioning/registry latency -> scale-up lag -> p95/p99 regression.

Ryan C: immediate mitigations we applied:
- bumped min_replicas for eu-dedicated-pool to 1 (from 0) at 09:28
- temporarily increased max_surge and enabled image pre-pull on newly provisioned instances
- added routing rule to steer critical traffic to fallback pool (hosted-high-throughput) for 5m

Sara L: Customer notified at 09:32 with ETA and temporary routing. They confirmed improved p95 after the changes.

Emily Z: customer reply: 'Thanks, saw big improvement. Could you make this non-blocking for us? We need guaranteed sub-500ms for chat.' They've asked for a long-term fix.

Maria P: long-term mitigation proposals:
- set min_replicas>=1 for Dedicated pools serving SLA customers, or a per-tenant warm-standby option
- implement image pre-pull during scale decision (start pulling image earlier) and initialize drivers in a pre-warm step
- reduce autoscaler decision cooldown or adopt predictive scaling for scheduled batch jobs
- add per-pool 'burst buffer' capacity that is cheaper (lower-priority warm instances) to absorb surges
- make a health check for cloud provisioning delays and failover quicker to alternate region/pool

Ryan C: also need to quantify cold-start token cost: measure driver init + model load per model variant and publish a warm-up profile. We can then use those profiles to adjust scale-up timing or pre-warm CPU-only workers.

Jordan M: ops action items I can own:
- increase min_replicas to 1 for all SLA-tagged dedicated pools (change pushed, doc number DOC-OPS-269)
- enable image pre-pull for EU for next 48h as trial

Maria P: SRE actions:
- update autoscaler policy to reduce conservative cooldown for dedicated pools (PR in flight: https://git.redwood.internal/pr/2387)
- add a dashboard alert: 'dedicated-pool scale-lag > 120s' and hook to runbook

Ryan C: runtime actions:
- implement 'warm init' container that can be started quicker (smaller image) to perform driver probe + kv-cache priming
- instrument and expose model warm time in metrics

Emily Z: support follow-up: will propose plan + cost impact to customer. Also recommend they avoid large batch blasts during business hours while we roll changes.

Alex K: summary + next steps: we've mitigated immediate customer impact by routing and increasing min_replicas. Root cause is configuration + cloud provisioning edge-case. Owners:
- Jordan: ops changes + image pre-pull (ETA 24h)
- Maria: autoscaler policy PR + alerting (ETA 48h)
- Ryan: warm-init prototype (ETA 1 week)
- Emily: customer comms and follow-up

Sara L: please add these to postmortem template. No P0 outage declared since degraded but customer impacted.

Emily Z: customer asked for an SLA assurance doc. I'll assemble a short write-up once we have permanent mitigations.

Alex K: closing notes: make sure we capture exact request id samples and any replay logs for more forensic analysis. Great quick cross-team response.

Ryan C: adding a small repro snippet I used in staging:

```
# repro burst against staging pool with min_replicas=0
for i in {1..200}; do curl -sS -X POST https://staging.api.redwood/v1/generate -d @payload.json &
done
# watch p95/p99 in grafana dashboard: infra/ingress->dedicated-eu
```

Maria P: I'll file the incident postmortem with timeline and attach the logs + metrics.

Jordan M: deploying pre-pull now to EU canary, will monitor image pull success rate and node ready time. ping if you see any regressions. :eyes:

Emily Z: customer confirmed improved performance at 10:05 UTC. Closing loop with them and will keep them in the loop about the permanent fixes.

Alex K: thanks team. We'll reconvene if anything else crops up.
